limitations: One trusted synthetic receiver/journal; no external arbitration, APPLIED revocation, diary-loss resolution, branches, variable metering or compensation.

Compose proves real UNKNOWN->APPLIED from the same journal and UNKNOWN->closed ABSENT for v1 suffix; the historical ABSENT/APPLIED contradiction fixture is SQL-owner evidence, not a valid receiver reopening a closed absence.

One settlement per operation/generation; later contradictory facts invalidate it and remain blocking without a superseding settlement. All-ABSENT without progress and reopening CANCELLED/COMPLETED are outside this increment.
v1 is limited to its calibrated two-step 4/6 fixture, its suffix and calibrated single-step SUCCESS. v2 Compose covers 3 steps/2 accounts, not every size up to 32/8.
Historical receipts without stored payload are not retroactively enriched: resolution proves the canonical receiver payload, retaining original bytes. Incompatible stored hashes remain blocked.
No unattended restart recovery or power-loss injection. Terminal local retirement and continuation rearming remain explicit.
SQL transaction guards do not promise physical commit deadlines across subsequent WAL/kernel/storage pauses.
No production provider/credentials, promotion, deployment outside disposable lab or D4 closure.
